Subject: Service-account ops alignment for observability connectors (Datadog / Grafana / OTLP)

Team / partners —

Thanks for jumping on this thread. We have several parallel efforts to onboard Datadog and Grafana ingestion for Redwood Private and Dedicated deployments, and we discovered some inconsistent expectations around service accounts, credential rotation, and least-privilege scoping. Before we lock a rollout pattern, I want to align on an ops/governance approach that satisfies: SOC 2 evidence capture, short-lived credentials where possible, scoped permissions for connector ingestion, and a repeatable provisioning flow our customers can run in cloud and air-gapped environments.

High-level asks:
- Can each partner confirm recommended identity pattern (static API key, scoped IAM role, token + rotation, or OIDC short-lived creds) and any constraints for on-prem or VPC deployments?
- We need a sample minimal permission set for each connector so our security team can validate least-privilege.
- Please review the attached provisioning guide (sa-provisioning-guide.pdf) and flag any gaps.
- Laura — please capture the mutual action plan once partners confirm.
- Grace & Neha — you’ll lead the security vetting for the permission matrix.
- Tessa — can you propose a 90-minute runbook workshop next week to validate a provisioning flow end-to-end?

Attachments: sa-provisioning-guide.pdf (proposed flow + YAML examples)

I’ll consolidate answers and propose a canonical pattern we can document in the partner playbook.

Ben

Subject: Re: Service-account ops alignment for observability connectors (Datadog / Grafana / OTLP)

Ben / all —

Thanks for the clear list. From Grafana Cloud / Grafana Agent perspective:
- Preferred pattern: short-lived credentials where possible. For cloud-hosted Grafana Cloud we recommend using token-based API keys with write-scoped permissions for metrics/logs (create:metrics_write). For self-hosted Grafana Agent talking to Loki/Tempo we recommend using scoped ingestion API keys or proxying through an authenticated OTLP gateway.
- IAM/OIDC: For AWS-hosted customers we commonly recommend an IAM role with OIDC federation and STS AssumeRole for short-lived credentials; that covers the rotation requirement without storing long-lived secrets.
- Minimal permission set (high level): metrics_write, logs_ingest, and agent_registration. We can provide a YAML snippet that maps to these actions for your provisioning guide.
- On-prem: short-lived creds are harder in air-gapped installs — typical approach is a locally provisioned service account with an offline rotation policy and an audit script to capture rotation events. We can provide a hardened checklist.

I’ll attach our recommended YAML mapping in a follow-up doc and link Grafana docs here: https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/authentication/

Tom Harris
Partner Engineering, Grafana Labs
tharris@grafana.com

From: Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@datadog.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Mar 2028 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service-account ops alignment for observability connectors (Datadog / Grafana / OTLP)

Ben —

Datadog’s guidance:
- For cloud agents we accept API keys with rotation; for managed ingestion (site-specific) using short-lived tokens via our API key rotation endpoints is recommended. We also support ingesting OTLP through our gateway; if you go OTLP -> Datadog, use TLS + mTLS for extra assurance in private deployments.
- Minimal permissions: events_write, metrics_submit, traces_ingest. If customers use host-level agents, they should provision a constrained API key (ingest-only).
- On-prem/VPC: we recommend running an internal OTLP relay with mTLS to Datadog’s gateway where possible. That eliminates long-lived public keys.

I attached an example OTLP bridge config we use in pilots (mamp-config.yaml). We can run a short workshop to validate the Helm chart + service account mapping.

Quick ask: can Redwood provide a single canonical permission matrix template that partners fill in? That will speed up the security triage.

—Priya

Strategic Partnerships, Datadog

2) Security review: Grace and Neha will validate the three example flows (Grafana token, Datadog ingest key, OTLP mTLS) and produce a short list of must-have audit checks for SOC 2 evidence capture.
3) Workshop: Tessa to schedule a 90-minute runbook workshop for next Tue/Thu (please indicate availability). Goal: provision a sample connector into our staging Dedicated cluster, validate ingestion, and exercise rotation.
4) On-prem guidance: Monitorly — can you sketch the offline rotation approach you use for air-gapped installs and share a one-page runbook?

Attached: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (starter MAM — Laura will update)

If this looks good I’ll convert into a short PR to our partner playbook and assign owners for the partner portal entries.

Ben
